- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
Line or code reference: review_dependency_proxy_ready function, lines 4115-4121
Problem: The readiness probe performs 30 iterations. Each iteration has a timeout 2 on docker exec and a 0.5s sleep after failure. The worst-case wall-clock wait when the proxy never becomes ready is at least 45 seconds (30 × ~1.5s) and up to 75 seconds (30 × 2.5s) depending on Docker responsiveness. The function would still return 1 after exhausting probes and the install would correctly fail, so the behavioral impact is nil. The probe count is conservative rather than incorrect.
Why it fails at runtime: Does not fail at runtime. The loop exits correctly to install_failed=true after all probes are exhausted. The only issue is the probe count is substantially larger than needed for a Python server that binds and writes a ready file in milliseconds; 5-10 iterations would achieve the same reliability at lower worst-case latency.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
Location: review_dependency_proxy_ready function, line 4117
Issue: 30 probe iterations with 2s timeout each is excessive for a local proxy that should start in under a second.
Suggested minimal fix: Reduce iteration count to 10 (seq 1 10) which still provides ~15s worst-case wait while keeping the existing 2s timeout and 0.5s sleep. The proxy is a local Python process, not a remote service; it either starts immediately or never starts.
Estimated lines changed: 1

Line or code reference: review_dependency_proxy_ready() at lines 4115-4121; AI editor summary in PR comment 5776854524
Problem: The AI editor's PR summary claims the new readiness gate "waits up to 15 seconds", but the implemented function performs 30 iterations × (2 s timeout + 0.5 s sleep) ≈ 75 s worst case when every probe times out. The on-record expectation operators will read into the comment does not match the actual bound enforced in code.
Why it fails at runtime: Not a runtime defect (the function correctly returns 1 after 30 attempts and the install continues with whatever state exists). The runtime failure is a documentation/transparency defect: an operator reading the AI summary would plan for a 15 s budget, then observe up to ~75 s of startup latency before pip runs — most visibly on slow runners where the python:3.12-slim image pull or container first start dominates.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

Line or code reference: review_dependency_proxy_ready() function, lines 4115-4121
Problem: The function performs 30 probe iterations with a 2-second timeout and 0.5-second sleep between attempts, resulting in a worst-case duration of approximately 75 seconds (30 × 2.5s). However, the editor summary in PR comment 5776854524 states the gate "waits up to 15 seconds before starting the dependency installer."
Why it fails at runtime: When every probe times out (proxy startup delay or resource contention), operators debugging installation failures will expect a 15-second bound based on the documented behavior, but the actual wait is 5× longer. This mismatch between documented and actual behavior can mislead troubleshooting and mask real proxy startup issues.
